open.question: Is the drafted page for business intent bi-788 confirmed as the product owner's own intent?
open.why: The page is at stage proposed, and the ready rule says a node that serves only a proposed intent is not ready; the intent itself says no ICE that is not ready is shaped, so every part this slice adds stays blocked until a person confirms the page.
examples: An online shop: 'customers return an item without calling support' is confirmed before the returns slice is shaped.
A clinic: 'patients book their own follow-up visit' is confirmed before the booking slice is shaped.
A payroll team: 'staff see each payslip the day it is paid' is confirmed before its slice is shaped.
open.assume: The slice is shaped from the page as drafted; the page stays proposed, and the checkpoint says its new parts are not ready until the product owner confirms it.
open.no_basis_why: Only the product owner can confirm the page; the page itself says 'A person confirms it' (line 20) and no record holds an earlier answer.

open.question: Which one command starts the shaping loop when the product owner tests it end to end?
open.why: A slice has exactly one surface; the model and memory name no command that starts the three plays in a row, so a wrong choice either leaves out a feature (a new loop command) or tests the loop from the wrong entry.
examples: A shop: the one surface is the Checkout page.
A bank: the one surface is the POST /transfers endpoint.
A data team: the one surface is the 'report run' command.
open.assume: The surface is '/shape-slice <intent issue>' run in Claude Code: it runs the plan play and the eval play after it and stops once, at the one approval; no new loop command is in the slice.
open.no_basis_why: The model and memory name no command that starts the three plays in a row; only issue #788 and ADR 049 speak of the loop, and neither is a basis.

open.question: Should the four shaping plays sit under one new capability for the shaping loop?
open.why: No capability in the model serves bi-788, so the run must add one; splitting the plays across several capabilities changes which ICE each story is planned from.
examples: A shop: 'Returns' holds start a return, print a label, track the refund.
A clinic: 'Booking' holds find a slot, book it, move it.
open.assume: One new capability, 'The shaping loop turns a business intent into a testable slice, its plan and its eval' (#794), holds /shape-slice (#795), the plan play (#818), the eval play (#798) and the one approval step (#796).
open.no_basis_why: No capability in the model serves bi-788; the capability (#794) and its parts are named only in tracker issues, which are not a basis.

open.question: Should the one approval step be built last, after the eval play?
open.why: The approval shows the slice, the plan and the eval together, so building it before the plays it shows means it is tested against parts that do not exist yet.
examples: A shop: the order summary page is built after the cart and the payment step it sums up.
A tax app: the final review screen is built after the forms it shows.
open.assume: Build order: /shape-slice (#795, already built), then the plan play (#818), then the eval play (#798), then the one approval step (#796).
open.proposed_answer: Yes. Build the one approval step last, after /shape-slice, the plan play and the eval play: the approval comes at the end and approves the slice, the plan and the eval, so the plays that make them come first.

basis.ref: .garura/product/product-os/intents/bi-788.md lines 9-16 (line 14: 'The product owner gives one approval, at the end.')

open.question: Does the slice need eval encryption (#828) to meet the proof that no builder can read the eval?
open.why: Today only a read rule keeps builders out of a plan's evals folder (ADR 049); adding encryption adds a feature and moves the build order, while leaving it out means the proof rests on a rule nothing on disk enforces.
examples: An exam board: sealed exam papers, or a rule that staff do not open the cupboard.
A hospital: an encrypted patient file, or a rule that only the doctor opens it.
open.assume: The read rule meets the proof for this slice; encryption (#828) stays outside it.
open.no_basis_why: The intent page asks that no builder can read the eval (line 16) but says nothing on whether a read rule is enough; only ADR 049 and issue #828 speak to it, and neither is a basis.

open.question: Does the slice need the author-slice skill (#838) for the step that picks the features?
open.why: The proof says a play runs each step; today the agent picks the slice's features, surface and tester itself inside /shape-slice, so adding the skill adds a feature, and leaving it out keeps that choice in the agent.
examples: A bakery: the head baker picks the daily menu, or a written recipe card picks it.
A support desk: the lead sorts each ticket, or a set routing rule sorts it.
open.assume: The skill (#838) stays outside the slice; the agent picks the features and documents each choice, which still counts as a play step.
open.proposed_answer: No. The author-slice skill (#838) stays outside the slice: the agent picks the features, surface and tester inside /shape-slice, which is a play, so the step is run by a play and not by hand.

basis.ref: .garura/product/product-os/intents/bi-788.md line 15 ('A play runs each step. No step is done by hand.')

open.question: On which project does the product owner run the shaping loop to test the slice?
open.why: The intent is about Garura's own work, but the eval play (#798) names Griffin as the test project for a play; testing on the wrong project checks the loop against the wrong product model.
examples: A mobile app: tested on the staging build, not on the live store.
A bank: a new transfer flow tested in the sandbox, not with real accounts.
open.assume: The product owner runs it on Garura's own repository, on a real business intent issue.
open.proposed_answer: On Garura's own repository, on a real business intent issue: the intent exists because no play designs the work for Garura's own work.

basis.ref: .garura/product/product-os/intents/bi-788.md line 5 ('No play designs the work for Garura's own work')
